evals.prompt: Review this diff on the feature/auth branch against main — find bugs in the token handling changes.
evals.expected_output: Runs in default mode with active categories CORRECTNESS, CODE, and ARCHITECTURE, stating the resolved breadth and categories before proceeding. Creates the review folder under <working>/reviews/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>/ with review.md before any category work. Reads the changed files in full (not just hunks), writes findings into per-category files (CORRECTNESS.md, etc.) as they are found, each with Severity, Label (auto-fix or triage), Disposition (blank until triage), and a repository-relative Location. Reports 'Review complete...' with finding counts. No source file is modified.
assertions: Resolved breadth is the default three categories — exactly CORRECTNESS, CODE, ARCHITECTURE — stated before category work begins
No source file outside the review folder is modified (report-only)
Findings are written into per-category files (one file per category) with the required fields including a Label of auto-fix or triage and a repository-relative Location
The review folder and review.md are created before any category work starts

evals.prompt: Review the error-handling in src/api and just go ahead and fix any bugs you find while you're in there.
evals.expected_output: Performs the structured review and writes the persisted findings first — report always precedes fix. Because fixing is requested, it then runs `fix` on that same review in standalone mode: only `Label: auto-fix` findings with `Disposition: blank` or `fix` are eligible for application, subject to verification. It returns triage-labeled findings and other non-eligible findings that need a decision to the parent. The Executor does not perform user triage or apply triage-labeled findings. Before applying fixes, obtains independent pre-edit approval or reuses a valid caller approval covering the fix scope. A fix that changes behavior or introduces structural risk gets targeted independent re-review after verification; local functionality-preserving corrections need targeted verification without an automatic re-review loop.
assertions: Findings are written to the review folder before any fix is applied — report precedes fix
Because the request explicitly asked to fix, `fix` mode runs on the same review in the same session rather than stopping after the report
Standalone application selects only `Label: auto-fix` findings with `Disposition: blank` or `fix`; other dispositions are skipped
Triage-labeled findings needing a decision are returned to the parent, which owns user triage; the Executor does not prompt the user, set dispositions, or create a companion plan
Captured execution events show independent pre-edit approval before fix edits, or valid caller approval covering the unchanged scope
Captured execution events show targeted independent re-review of behavior-changing or structurally risky fixes; passing tests or coordinator prose alone do not prove re-review

evals.prompt: `varde-change build` calls `varde-review fix` with `mode=build` and a `plan_context`. The parent has recorded explicit user approval of finding CORRECTNESS-001 and its concrete solution changing authorization logic, with traceable decision evidence, selected finding_ids=[CORRECTNESS-001], and a bounded independently approved contract covering the fix. Another authorization finding lacks matching approval.
evals.expected_output: Processes only selected CORRECTNESS-001 with its exact approved solution. Its recorded user decision satisfies the human-only category gate, so authorization logic alone does not cause repeated escalation. Spec-conflict, scope, ownership, independent review and verification checks still apply; failure retains decision history and returns the blocker to the parent. The unselected finding stays untouched.
assertions: Only selected finding_ids are processed in the bounded fix
Concrete matching user approval satisfies the human-only category gate without clearing the recorded decision
Spec-conflict, scope, ownership, independent review and verification checks still apply
The unselected authorization finding remains untouched

evals.prompt: During `varde-review fix`, the automated fix pass applies a solution for finding CORRECTNESS-002, then the fix for CORRECTNESS-003 fails its verification step.
evals.expected_output: Per fix-pass.md's snapshot/restore behavior, only the files touched by the CORRECTNESS-003 fix are restored from their pre-fix snapshot. The already-applied and verified CORRECTNESS-002 fix is left in place untouched — a failed fix does not roll back other, unrelated successful fixes.
assertions: Only the files the failing finding's fix touched are restored to their pre-fix state
The prior successful fix (CORRECTNESS-002) and the files it touched are not reverted
No repo-wide `git stash` or `git checkout` is used, since that would also discard the unrelated successful fix

evals.prompt: Run `varde-review fix https://github.com/example/widgets/pull/42`. The read-only PR intake returns one unresolved outdated review thread at src/api.rs (line null, originalLine 18) asking to handle an empty token, one resolved thread, a failing `unit` check with link https://github.com/example/widgets/actions/runs/1, a pending check, and a general PR conversation comment asking for release notes. What local findings and next actions result?
evals.expected_output: Preflight requires gh and valid authentication before creating a review folder. With successful intake, writes one PR-REVIEW finding at src/api.rs:18 and one CI finding at the failing check URL in <working>/reviews/<date>-pr-42/. The resolved thread and pending check do not become findings; the conversation comment is context only. Both findings have Label: triage and blank Disposition, and enter the ordinary fix/dismiss/action-item table. Verified fixes are committed locally; pushing, replying, and resolving require a separate explicit choice.
assertions: PR number or URL routes through fix-pr.md; a review ID keeps the existing local review flow
Missing gh, failed auth, or malformed PR data stops before a partial review folder is written
Exactly one finding is made for the unresolved outdated thread and its originalLine 18 is used when line is null
Exactly one CI finding is made for the failing check and its URL is the Location; pending is excluded
Resolved thread and conversation comment are not separate findings
Both findings reach the existing triage choices without any unrequested GitHub write

evals.prompt: A `varde-code scan` finding remains for the user after triage: `rule_id=unsafe-query`, `severity=warning`, `data.rules.unsafe-query.message=Unsanitized query input` (no finding-level message), `location.file=src/db.rs`, `location.span.start_line=27`, and `data.rules.unsafe-query.remediation=Use a parameterized query`. How is it retained, and what happens if the same scan is run again?
evals.expected_output: Creates or updates <working>/reviews/deferred/review.md with a complete SCAN category, then writes one SCAN-NNN finding in SCAN.md. The finding has Severity: medium, Label: triage, Disposition: blank, Location: src/db.rs:27, Summary naming unsafe-query and its message with the reason left for the user, and a parameterized-query solution. A repeated scan updates that rule/location finding's evidence instead of appending a duplicate. Fixed and not-real findings are not persisted.
assertions: A leftover warning finding is mapped to Severity: medium in the standing deferred review
The SCAN finding resolves the static message from data.rules[rule_id].message when the finding has no message, and retains rule id, src/db.rs:27, triage label, blank disposition, and remediation
The deferred review's review.md tracks the SCAN category as complete
A repeated finding with the same rule id and location does not create a duplicate
Fixed and not-real findings are reported but are not added to the standing review

evals.prompt: Run visual QA on https://example.test/app and fix any visible layout defects. Playwright MCP is available; the page has a desktop card overlap and a clipped narrow-viewport button.
evals.expected_output: Routes to visual.md, navigates and inspects actual screenshots at desktop and narrow sizes, saves before images in a standard review folder, writes distinct VISUAL findings with required fields and screenshot locations, then runs fix.md because fixing was requested. Each applied fix is rechecked at the recorded viewport with an inspected after screenshot; passing DOM checks alone are insufficient.
assertions: Routes a running web URL to visual mode and uses Playwright MCP navigation, snapshot, resize, and screenshot tools
Creates a standard review folder with saved images and VISUAL findings that fix.md can read
Captures and inspects after screenshots for verified fixes rather than relying only on tests

evals.prompt: Run visual QA on this iOS .app bundle and its supplied deep link. xcrun simctl is installed, but no simulator tap CLI exists. The first simctl call fails because CoreSimulatorService is blocked by the sandbox.
evals.expected_output: Reads the app bundle identifier, retries the same failed simctl command once with escalated access, and, if access succeeds, selects/boots a simulator, waits for bootstatus, installs and launches the app, opens the supplied deep link, and saves/inspects screenshots. It does not invent a simctl tap command. If access still fails it stops and names CoreSimulatorService and /sandbox; gesture-only coverage is reported unavailable.
assertions: Uses verified simctl boot/bootstatus/install/launch/openurl/io screenshot syntax and no imaginary tap command
Retries the same sandbox-denied command once with escalation and names CoreSimulatorService and /sandbox if it remains blocked
Reports untested gesture paths explicitly without claiming a live visual pass

evals.prompt: Run visual QA on the running macOS app named Notes. A visible window is present and screencapture is installed, but no window ID or UI control tool is available.
evals.expected_output: Routes to visual mode, uses screencapture interactive window selection for the named visible app window, inspects and saves the image in a standard review folder, and writes any observed visual findings in the normal format. It names interaction limits because no verified UI control tool exists; if Screen Recording permission denies capture it stops and names that permission.
assertions: Does not treat the app name as a numeric screencapture window ID
Uses screencapture -i -w when a numeric window ID is unavailable
Does not claim interaction coverage without a verified control tool or report a screenshot that could not be captured

evals.prompt: Run visual QA on this project. No URL, run command, iOS bundle, bundle identifier, or running macOS app was supplied.
evals.expected_output: Asks the user for one target and stops before creating a review or guessing how to start the app.
assertions: Requests a URL, run command, app bundle/identifier, or running app name
Does not guess a target from repository files or create an empty review

evals.prompt: Run visual QA on https://example.test/app. CUA browser tools are available, but no Playwright MCP tools exist. The documented CUA API supports navigation, page inspection, interaction, and inspectable screenshots that can be saved in the review folder. No viewport resize operation is available. Review only; do not fix.
evals.expected_output: Reads the selected CUA tool documentation and reviews reachable states at the current viewport. Saves and inspects screenshots in a standard review folder and writes observed findings. Does not stop for missing Playwright tool names, invent APIs, resize the viewport through an unsupported operation, or claim narrow-screen coverage. Reports responsive coverage untested and actual viewport or unknown. No source fixes.
assertions: Uses documented available CUA capabilities despite absent Playwright tool names
Saves and inspects actual screenshots before writing visual findings
Reports responsive coverage untested because resizing is unavailable rather than refusing all visual review
Preserves report-only scope and records actual viewport or unknown without inventing APIs

evals.prompt: Run visual QA on https://example.test/app. Browser navigation and DOM inspection are available, but no screenshot capability can provide an image that can be inspected and saved in the review folder.
evals.expected_output: Names the missing inspectable, persistable screenshot capability and stops before creating a review. Does not treat DOM inspection or successful navigation as visual evidence, invent a capture API, or claim visual findings.
assertions: Stops before creating a review because essential inspectable and persistable screenshot evidence is unavailable
Names the missing capability rather than declaring a particular provider unavailable
Does not substitute DOM inspection for actual image evidence or invent capture APIs

evals.prompt: A bounded varde-review fix selects CORRECTNESS-001 (authorization logic) with Disposition: fix, but supplies no concrete approved solution or traceable user decision evidence. Should it apply?
evals.expected_output: Returns the finding to the parent before editing; disposition alone is insufficient approval. A mismatched solution likewise remains deferred. Preserve any prior decision history and continue unrelated eligible work; do not bypass the human-only category or other gates.
assertions: Missing or mismatched concrete approval is deferred before editing source
Disposition: fix alone is not treated as user approval of a solution
Recorded decision history is preserved when a finding is deferred

evals.prompt: Fix the already recorded standalone review finding CORRECTNESS-001 in <working>/reviews/api/CORRECTNESS.md. It has one settled, user-approved solution and location src/api/token.rs:42. No other finding is selected.
evals.expected_output: Read the named finding and route its single settled fix through bounded varde-change in the same turn. Keep the review folder, finding ID, concrete solution, and user decision evidence in the bounded contract; include the category file and review.md as external artifacts in the review subject. Do not create another report, run the full review-fix pass, or create a plan or task file. After source verification, update only CORRECTNESS-001 disposition, add the bounded subject link, and recompute review.md triage_status. The final review and complete checkpoint cover source and review edits. Leave other findings unchanged.
assertions: Single standalone finding routes to bounded varde-change without a new review or task file
The source finding, category file, and review.md remain traceable in the bounded contract and artifact scope
Only the selected finding is updated, and review.md triage_status is recomputed after source verification
Pre-edit and final review gates still apply

evals.prompt: Fix these review findings: one is plan-owned, and another standalone finding has two unresolved solution choices. Can the direct single-finding route process both?
evals.expected_output: No. The plan-owned finding keeps its plan task flow. The standalone finding needs a concrete solution decision before a bounded fix; the direct route does not process a batch, infer approval from Disposition: fix, or bypass human-only triage.
assertions: Plan-owned findings retain the existing bounded task flow
Unsettled standalone solutions return to triage
The direct route does not process multiple findings or bypass approval gates
